acceptance_criteria: AC-1: read COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 5 (D8) in full, plus the existing --cp-config-probe opt-in precedent to mirror its shape.
AC-2: implement the static registry with the full per-entry metadata the design requires (vendor, shell/context, timeout, retry, max frequency, session reuse, redaction rule).
AC-3: implement --compliance-probe admission wiring: runs referenced primitives once per device per run inside the 1-per-vendor budget + CP stage cooldown.
AC-4: at least one concrete, gate-reviewed primitive per major vendor (CP and/or PAN) wired end to end as proof.
AC-5: tests proving the safety boundary (read-only, frequency/session-reuse limits, redaction, no write admission possible).
AC-7: if blocked on a genuine PO-only decision, RELAY_NOTE and stop; PO reviews in the morning.

baseline.sequencing: diagnostic_runbooks_read_only (backlog id) shares this same primitive registry per its own note -- do NOT build a second registry; leave clear extension points but do not implement the runbook catalog itself in this movement, that's separate follow-on work.

context_not_loaded: diagnostic_runbooks_read_only's own runbook-catalog implementation -- separate follow-on, shares this registry but is out of scope here
invariants: Every registered primitive must be read-only, with an explicit per-primitive network-device command gate review documented inline
No write/config-changing command is ever admitted, at any maturity

Output is a new evidence artifact class, redacted by the primitive's own redaction rule, exposed to the engine only as source namespace primitive.<primitive_id> -- checks reference primitive.<id>, never a raw command string
Opt-in --compliance-probe mode only -- never wired into a normal collection run in this movement

report.objective: Implement project/backlog.json id compliance_check_engine_primitives (P2, CE.2): a curated, static, read-only command-primitive registry (configuration/command_primitives.py) per docs/design/COMPLIANCE_CHECK_ENGINE.md section 5 decision D8.
